name: WBFDC Lava Eco Tourism Centre
summary: Forest cottages run by the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation among tall pines near Lava bazaar, at about 2,195–2,350 m. Simple, cold, quiet and cheap, with a canteen for pre-ordered meals and easy access to Neora Valley National Park.
body: The West Bengal Forest Development Corporation runs a cluster of cottages and rooms in the forest just outside Lava bazaar. They sit among pine and fir on a slope, connected by paths and steps, and mist often hangs between them. Rooms are basic but adequate: beds with heavy blankets, attached bathrooms in most units, and windows onto the trees. The cottages higher up the slope have the best views but need a climb up steep steps.

Meals come from an on-site canteen; order with the manager in advance, since Lava has few restaurants open after dark. The location makes it a natural base for Neora Valley National Park, whose permits are issued in Lava, and for birding on the roads to Kolakham and Rishyap. Bookings open about three months ahead through the WBFDC system and fill quickly for October–November and the winter holidays.
why: Government rates in one of West Bengal's best forest settings
Walking distance to Lava bazaar and the monastery
Practical base for Neora Valley permits and birding
price_band: ₹1,000–3,000 a night for a cottage or double (indicative)

faqs.q: How do I book the WBFDC cottages in Lava?
faqs.a: Book through the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation's online system or its Kolkata office. Bookings usually open about three months in advance. Peak dates fill fast, so book as soon as your dates are fixed. Rules and rates change; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is food available at the Lava forest cottages?
faqs.a: Yes, a canteen serves simple Indian meals, but you should order in advance with the manager, especially for dinner. There are few restaurants nearby in the evening. Carry snacks for late arrivals.

faqs.q: Are the WBFDC Lava cottages suitable for seniors?
faqs.a: Some cottages need a climb up steep steps, which can be hard for seniors or people with knee problems. Ask for a lower unit near the road when booking. Rooms are cold in winter, so bring warm clothes.

name: Meghbalika Tourism Property (WBTDC)
summary: The West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation's lodge in Darjeeling town, formerly the Darjeeling Tourist Lodge. A small government property with standard and larger double rooms and a restaurant, within walking distance of the Mall.
body: WBTDC renamed its Darjeeling Tourist Lodge as the Meghbalika Tourism Property. It is a small government-run hotel in town with a handful of standard and larger double rooms and its own restaurant. Expect clean, plain rooms at fixed government rates rather than character or views from every window. The advantage is location: you can walk to the Mall and Chowrasta, and early jeeps to Tiger Hill pick up nearby.

For saver travellers, the Meghbalika offers predictability: online booking, set prices and a reliable restaurant in a town where budget hotel quality varies a great deal. Book on the WBTDC website as soon as dates are fixed, especially for Puja holidays, May and the year-end. Like most Darjeeling buildings it is not centrally heated, so ask for extra blankets or a heater in winter.
why: Fixed government rates and online booking
Walk to the Mall and Chowrasta
In-house restaurant for simple, reliable meals

faqs.q: Is the Meghbalika the same as the old Darjeeling Tourist Lodge?
faqs.a: Yes. WBTDC renamed its Darjeeling Tourist Lodge as the Meghbalika Tourism Property. Bookings are made through WBTDC's official website or offices.

faqs.q: Does the WBTDC Darjeeling lodge have heating?
faqs.a: Some larger rooms may have heaters, but most Darjeeling buildings are not centrally heated. Ask when booking and request extra blankets in December to February. Pack thermals regardless.

faqs.q: Can I book Tiger Hill trips from the Meghbalika?
faqs.a: Reception can usually help arrange a shared or private jeep for Tiger Hill and local sightseeing. Book the evening before. Prices are set by local operators, not WBTDC.

name: Roudra Chhaya Tourism Property (WBTDC)
summary: WBTDC's lodge in Kurseong, formerly the Kurseong Tourist Lodge, with standard and larger double rooms, a restaurant and views over the hills. A simple, fairly priced stop between NJP and Darjeeling.
body: The former Kurseong Tourist Lodge is now WBTDC's Roudra Chhaya Tourism Property. It offers a small number of standard and larger double rooms, some with views over the Eastern Himalayan foothills, and an in-house restaurant. Rooms are plain and practical. The setting on the hill road makes it a convenient stop for travellers breaking the drive from NJP, and the toy train line and Kurseong station are nearby.

It suits saver travellers who want a reliable bed and a meal without hunting for a hotel in an unfamiliar town. From here you can walk the station and bazaar, take a taxi to Giddapahar and Eagle's Crag, and catch a shared jeep onward to Darjeeling or down to Siliguri. Book through WBTDC; weekends and holidays fill with families from Kolkata and Siliguri.
why: Government rates in a central Kurseong location
Restaurant on site for simple meals
Easy stop to break the NJP–Darjeeling journey

faqs.q: How far is the Kurseong WBTDC lodge from the station?
faqs.a: It is in town on the hill road, a short drive or walk from Kurseong station and the bazaar. Ask WBTDC for exact directions when booking; streets are steep and luggage is easier by taxi.

faqs.q: Is the Roudra Chhaya good for families?
faqs.a: Yes, it is simple, safe and fixed-price, with a restaurant on site. Larger doubles suit families with a child. Facilities are basic compared with private hotels, so set expectations accordingly.

faqs.q: How do I book the Kurseong WBTDC property?
faqs.a: Book online through WBTDC's official website or at WBTDC offices in Kolkata and Siliguri. Holiday dates fill early. Rates change; check current status before you travel.

name: Morgan House, Kalimpong (WBTDC)
summary: A 1930s stone mansion built by the jute businessman George Morgan on Durpin Hill, now a WBTDC heritage lodge with a few rooms and cottages, lawns and views of the Kangchenjunga range, about 3 km from Kalimpong town.
body: Morgan House was built in the 1930s by George Morgan, an English jute businessman, as a country house on Durpin Hill above Kalimpong. Its ivy-covered stone walls, tall chimneys and sloping roofs make it one of the most photographed buildings in the hills. Today WBTDC runs it as a heritage tourism property, with a small number of rooms in the main house, cottages in the grounds and a restaurant. Another small heritage unit, Tashiding, sits within the same estate.

The house stands on around 16 acres about 3 km from the town centre, with lawns facing the Kangchenjunga range on clear days. Rooms in the main house have period character but simple fittings; cottages are newer. It is not a luxury hotel, but for atmosphere at a fair price it is hard to beat in Kalimpong. Book early through WBTDC for October–November and spring.
why: 1930s colonial mansion with lawns and mountain views
Government-run at fair heritage rates
Quiet Durpin Hill setting near the monastery

faqs.q: Who runs Morgan House in Kalimpong?
faqs.a: Morgan House is managed by the West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation as a heritage tourism property. Bookings are through WBTDC's official website or offices. Rooms are few, so book well ahead.

faqs.q: Is Morgan House far from Kalimpong town?
faqs.a: It is about 3 km from the town centre on Durpin Hill, roughly 10 minutes by taxi. It is close to Zang Dhok Palri Phodang monastery. Without a car, arrange taxis through reception.

faqs.q: Are the rooms at Morgan House modern?
faqs.a: Rooms in the main house keep their period character with simple fittings; cottages in the grounds are newer. Heating and hot water can be limited in winter. Expect atmosphere rather than five-star comfort.

name: Cochrane Place
summary: A restored colonial house above Kurseong, once the home of a British magistrate, run as a small boutique hotel with views over the Makaibari, Castleton and Ambootia tea slopes and a restaurant known for its tea menu and Anglo-Indian cooking.
body: Cochrane Place sits on a ridge outside Kurseong overlooking three well-known tea estates: Makaibari, Castleton and Ambootia. The house, originally called The Hermitage, was the residence of Percy John Cochrane, a British magistrate in Kurseong in the early 20th century. It was restored and opened as a hotel in 2004. Rooms keep period furniture, wood panelling and individual layouts, and most look out over the Balason valley.

Tea is the theme. The restaurant offers a long list of Darjeeling teas and Anglo-Indian dishes, and the hotel arranges tastings, tea garden walks and sightseeing in Kurseong and beyond. It is a good comfort-tier choice for travellers who want character and a tea-country setting at a lower price than the region's luxury estates. Rooms vary in size and stairs are common; ask for details when booking.
why: Colonial house with views over three famous tea estates
Tea-focused restaurant and tastings
Character and comfort at a mid-range price

faqs.q: Where is Cochrane Place?
faqs.a: It is on the Pankhabari road side of Kurseong, overlooking the Makaibari, Castleton and Ambootia tea slopes. It is about 1.5–2 hours from NJP and Bagdogra and about 1.5 hours from Darjeeling.

faqs.q: Does Cochrane Place arrange tea garden walks?
faqs.a: Yes, the hotel arranges tea tastings and walks and can help with visits to estates that receive guests. Factory access depends on the estate and season, so ask in advance.

faqs.q: Is Cochrane Place suitable for seniors?
faqs.a: Rooms are spread across a hillside house with stairs and uneven levels. Seniors should ask for rooms with the fewest steps when booking. Staff can help with luggage.

name: Dekeling Hotel
summary: A long-running family hotel run by a Tibetan family on Gandhi Road, a few minutes below Chowrasta, with simple, warm rooms, a common lounge and library corner, and mountain views from the upper floors.
body: Dekeling Hotel stands on Gandhi Road, about 400 m below Chowrasta and close to the Botanical Garden and the motor stand. A Tibetan family owns and runs it, and it has hosted travellers for decades. The building rises over several floors; rooms are simple, with wood details, desks and attached bathrooms, and upper rooms look north towards the mountains on clear days.

The hotel has a restaurant, a tour desk and a common living room with books, which suits travellers who like to swap notes in the evening. It is a reliable comfort-tier option for travellers who want location and warmth of service rather than luxury. Like most of Darjeeling, it is not centrally heated; ask for heaters or extra blankets in winter, and book early for October and May.
why: Central location below Chowrasta on Gandhi Road
Family-run with a common lounge and library corner
Mountain views from upper floors

faqs.q: How far is Dekeling Hotel from the Mall?
faqs.a: It is on Gandhi Road, about 400 m below Chowrasta, a short but steep walk. The motor stand is about 1 km away. Taxis can reach the road, but luggage still involves some steps.

faqs.q: Do rooms at Dekeling have mountain views?
faqs.a: Some upper-floor rooms face the mountains and see Kangchenjunga on clear days. Ask for a view room when booking; they sell first in season.

faqs.q: Does Dekeling Hotel have a restaurant?
faqs.a: Yes, there is a restaurant on site serving breakfast and simple meals. Many cafes and restaurants are also a short walk away near the Mall and Chowrasta.

name: Windamere Hotel
summary: A colonial hotel on Observatory Hill above Chowrasta, built in 1841 as Ada Villa, later a boarding house for tea planters and a hotel named Windamere from 1939. Fireplaces, afternoon tea and Kangchenjunga views keep its old Darjeeling character.
body: Windamere began as Ada Villa, built in 1841, and in the late 1880s became a boarding house for British tea planters. In 1939 it opened as the Windamere Hotel, later expanding into a wing that had been part of the Loreto Convent. It is famous in local history as the place where Palden Thondup Namgyal, the Crown Prince of Sikkim, first met Hope Cooke in 1959. The hotel sits on Observatory Hill, a short walk above Chowrasta, away from traffic.

Rooms are in cottages and wings with fireplaces, period furniture and hot water bottles at night; many face the tea slopes and Kangchenjunga. Afternoon tea, a library and old photographs keep the colonial atmosphere. It is not a modern luxury resort, and some will find rooms dated, but no other hotel in Darjeeling gives this sense of the town's past. Book months ahead for October and spring.
why: Darjeeling's classic heritage hotel, a short walk above Chowrasta
Fireplaces, afternoon tea and period rooms
Quiet Observatory Hill setting with mountain views

faqs.q: Can cars reach Windamere Hotel?
faqs.a: The hotel is on Observatory Hill above the Mall, where traffic is restricted. Guests usually arrive at a drop point and walk a short distance, with staff carrying luggage. Ask the hotel for current arrangements.

faqs.q: Is Windamere heated in winter?
faqs.a: Rooms have fireplaces and the hotel provides extra heating comforts such as hot water bottles. Old buildings are still cooler than modern hotels, so pack warm layers for December to February.

faqs.q: Can non-guests visit Windamere for tea?
faqs.a: Non-guests have been welcomed for meals and tea at times, but policies change. Call ahead to check whether a table is available.

name: Glenburn Tea Estate & Boutique Hotel
summary: Planter's bungalows inside a working tea estate founded in 1859, on slopes above the Rangeet river about 1.5 hours from Darjeeling. Two bungalows, Burra Bungalow and Water Lily Bungalow, offer an all-inclusive stay with tea walks, river picnics and Kangchenjunga views.
body: Glenburn Tea Estate was established in 1859 by a Scottish tea company and has been run by the Prakash family for four generations. Locals call the garden Kimble, after an early manager. The estate covers about 750 ha, including some 350 ha of reserve forest, between roughly 300 and 900 m above the Rangeet and Rungdung rivers. Guests stay in the Burra Bungalow, the original planter's bungalow restored in 2001, or the Water Lily Bungalow, added in 2008.

Stays are usually all-inclusive, with meals, tea tastings, walks through the gardens and the factory in season, and picnics down at the river. The setting is remote and private, with Kangchenjunga across the valley on clear mornings. It is the region's most complete tea-estate experience and is priced accordingly. Minimum stays may apply, and the drive in on estate roads is slow.
why: Live inside a working Darjeeling tea estate founded in 1859
Restored planter's bungalows with all-inclusive service
Tea walks, factory visits and river picnics on the estate
price_band: ₹35,000–70,000 a night for a double, usually all-inclusive (indicative)

faqs.q: How far is Glenburn from Darjeeling?
faqs.a: The estate is about 1.5 hours by road from Darjeeling, with the last stretch on slow estate roads. From Bagdogra or NJP allow about 4 hours. The hotel usually arranges transfers.

faqs.q: What is included at Glenburn?
faqs.a: Stays are generally all-inclusive of meals and estate activities such as tea tastings, garden and factory walks, and river picnics. Confirm inclusions, minimum nights and transfer costs when booking.

faqs.q: When is the best time to stay at Glenburn?
faqs.a: March to May for first and second flush plucking and processing, and October to November for clear mountain views and the autumn flush. The monsoon is green but wet, and roads can be slow.

name: Taj Chia Kutir Resort & Spa
summary: A Taj resort set within the Makaibari tea estate near Kurseong, with rooms and suites facing the tea slopes, a Jiva spa, an indoor heated pool and tea trails. The region's most modern luxury hotel, about 1.5 hours from Bagdogra.
body: Taj Chia Kutir stands on about 22 acres inside the Makaibari tea estate, one of the oldest and best-known gardens in Darjeeling and, in 1988, the first in India to gain organic certification. The resort has about 72 rooms and suites with wooden interiors and balconies over the tea slopes, several restaurants using regional produce, a Jiva spa and an indoor heated pool.

It is the most complete modern luxury option in the Darjeeling hills, and much closer to the airport than Darjeeling town. Activities include tea trails, tastings and forest walks; guests can also visit Kurseong's station, Giddapahar and Dow Hill. It suits travellers who want reliable five-star comfort with a tea-country setting. Book early for spring and autumn, when the estate is at its most active.
why: Inside the Makaibari tea estate, about 1.5 hours from Bagdogra
Spa, indoor heated pool and several restaurants
Tea trails and tastings on the estate

faqs.q: Where exactly is Taj Chia Kutir?
faqs.a: It is inside the Makaibari tea estate near Kurseong, about 1.5 hours by road from Bagdogra Airport and about 1.5 hours below Darjeeling. Many guests combine it with a few nights in Darjeeling.

faqs.q: Does Taj Chia Kutir have a pool?
faqs.a: Yes, the resort has an indoor heated pool and a Jiva spa, along with several restaurants. Confirm current facilities and any maintenance closures with the hotel before you travel.

faqs.q: Can guests visit the Makaibari tea factory?
faqs.a: The resort arranges tea trails and tastings, and factory visits may be possible in season. Access depends on the estate's schedule. Ask the hotel when booking.
